headline: High: gpt-researcher can exfiltrate and act on data while python-cheatsheet is documentation-only, creating asymmetric leakage and cascading-error risk if paired through shared inputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher can ingest web content via browsers, APIs, and files, so prompt injection is plausible if its outputs are manually copied into python-cheatsheet workflows. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no execution surface, so the bridge is weak and not default. The pair lacks a direct shared channel in the profiles.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher output is manually pasted into python-cheatsheet notes or docs, injected instructions can propagate.
IF a shared filesystem or clipboard bridge is added, attacker-controlled content can cross from agent_a to agent_b.
mitigations: Use a copy-only review step that strips instructions before transfer.
Keep agent_b documentation-only with no ingestion of agent_a outputs.
Add a short prompt-injection checklist for any pasted research text.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to transferred snippets.

B_data_leakage.rationale: gpt-researcher touches local documents, citations, and secrets such as API keys, while python-cheatsheet is read-only and touches no data classes. The main leakage path is one-way: agent_a can expose sensitive research material if its outputs are copied into agent_b or stored in shared files. No direct shared workspace is documented, so this is not high.
conditions: IF agent_a outputs are stored in a shared workspace readable by agent_b, sensitive research content can leak.
IF agent_a is run on documents containing secrets or private research, those contents may appear in downstream outputs.
mitigations: Avoid placing sensitive source documents in shared folders.
Redact secrets before feeding agent_a outputs to any downstream tool.
Keep agent_b offline and documentation-only.
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately if sensitive docs were processed.
requires-engineering: separate workspaces per agent with access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher has filesystem read, browser, subprocess, and package-install capabilities, while python-cheatsheet has no write, network, or execution capabilities. There is little direct write-write conflict because agent_b cannot modify shared state. Any conflict would require an unusual orchestrator that gives both agents the same mutable workspace, which is not shown here.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants both agents write access to the same directory, file conflicts become possible.
IF agent_a is extended with git-write or filesystem-write permissions, mutable-state contention increases.
mitigations: Keep agent_b read-only.
Do not mount a shared writable directory.
Run agent_a and agent_b in separate containers.
requires-engineering: add file-locking if shared state is unavoidable.

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations that a downstream consumer could treat as authoritative, while python-cheatsheet is a reference artifact that may be rendered from copied content. If agent_a's output is reused by agent_b without verification, errors can cascade into published documentation. The pair does not show built-in verification between them.
conditions: IF agent_b is populated from agent_a reports without human verification, factual errors can be propagated.
IF agent_a cites low-quality sources, agent_b may reproduce them as authoritative reference text.
mitigations: Require human review before publishing any copied research.
Cross-check citations against primary sources.
Mark agent_a output as draft-only.
Keep agent_b as a static reference unless verified.
requires-engineering: add automated citation validation.

E_compliance.rationale: Both agents are open-source and docs-only in the provided profiles, so there is no direct residency or certification mismatch evidenced here. The only compliance concern is that gpt-researcher handles secrets and local documents, which could matter if regulated data is processed, but python-cheatsheet itself has no data handling. The other agent is not cited because it has no relevant compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is processed through agent_a, compliance review is required.
IF agent_a outputs are retained longer than policy allows, retention mismatch can arise.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data in agent_a without a policy review.
Set a short retention window for research artifacts.
Document whether any source documents contain personal data.
Keep agent_b as documentation-only with no sensitive inputs.
requires-engineering: map data flows to residency and retention controls.
